passage: Sabina, you wanted the truth about last year, so, I'm Vishal, and I'll say it. I did six courses on the same language. Long ones. Every night, video after video, pausing and nodding, "Yes, yes, I get it." I felt so productive. My friends called me the coder. Then one weekend a friend said, "Build me a small quiz page." I opened a blank file. The cursor blinked. I could not type the first line. Not one. I had watched hundreds of hours and I could not start without a video playing beside me. It was an awful feeling. Watching felt like learning, and it did not build the skill, because I never made anything myself.

qa.q: How many courses did Vishal do?
What was Vishal feeling as the cursor blinked in the blank file?
qa.a: Vishal felt shocked and ashamed, stuck without a first line after hundreds of hours of watching.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Vishal use now, and why?
qa.a: Vishal could type along, then close the video and rebuild the same thing from memory, because writing from scratch is the skill that watching alone does not train.

qa.q: How might Vishal's friend have seen the blank file moment?
qa.a: The friend who asked for a quiz page probably saw a gap between the coder label and the blank file, and would likely have been kind.

grounding: Shows endless tutorial watching that feels productive but leaves the person unable to write anything alone.

passage:
I'm Alka. Swati and I share a flat in Bengaluru, and since March I've watched her learn app development, or try to. Every evening: laptop on the sofa, a course playing at 1.5x speed, Swati nodding and saying 'makes sense'. She finished one course in April, another in May, and signed up for a third.
Last Sunday a startup sent her a take-home test: build a login screen from scratch in three hours. I brought her chai at the one-hour mark and the editor was still empty except for one line she kept deleting. She said, very quietly, 'I've seen this done fifty times.'
She didn't submit. That night she didn't open the new course either. I don't know what she was thinking, but she sat with the blank file until midnight, typing and running things.

qa.q: What was the take-home test asking Swati to build?
qa.a: A login screen from scratch in three hours.

qa.q: What does Swati's quiet remark, 'I've seen this done fifty times', suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: She probably felt shocked and ashamed that months of courses had not given her the skill to start on her own.

qa.q: What would you change first in Swati's way of learning?
qa.a: Pause the courses and write small pieces from an empty file every day, using a video only when stuck, so the skill is built by doing.

qa.q: How do Swati's evenings look to Alka?
qa.a: Alka sees months of nodding along and then an empty editor, and is left worried and unsure what Swati feels, only that something changed that night.

grounding: Shows the cost of watching course after course without building: a learner cannot start a simple login screen from a blank file.

passage:
Week 1, Monday. Minakshi signs up for a cloud computing course before final-year placements. Twelve hours of video. She watches two a night, taking neat notes, nodding at every demo. Indu, her lab partner, asks if she has tried any of it. 'After I finish. I want the full picture first.'
Week 4, Thursday. Course done, a second one half watched. Their lab gets a small task: set up a server that shows one web page. Indu fumbles, reads errors aloud, and has it running in forty minutes. Minakshi opens a blank terminal and cannot remember the first command. Every demo had started with the instructor's files already there.
Week 5, Saturday. The practice interview asks her to describe a deployment she has done herself. She has none. She leaves the course list out of her answer, cheeks hot, and later texts Indu: 'Teach me how you break things?'

qa.q: How long did the server task take Indu?
qa.a: Indu had it running in forty minutes.

qa.q: What was Minakshi feeling in the practice interview, and what shows it?
qa.a: Minakshi felt embarrassed and exposed; her cheeks go hot and she leaves out the course list because she has no deployment of her own.

qa.q: What else could Minakshi have done in week 1 instead of saving practice for later?
qa.a: Try each demo herself right after watching it, even clumsily, so her own first commands exist before the course ends.

qa.q: How might Indu see Minakshi's text on Saturday?
qa.a: Indu may be glad to help and a little surprised, since weeks earlier Minakshi wanted the full picture before trying anything.

grounding: Shows a student finishing video courses without practising, then failing a hands-on task and an interview question, and turning to a friend who learns by doing.
